_readme: Set 115 Session 1 — the cross-language parity corpus for session-title
resolution.
Two implementations resolve a session's title: the router's writer
(ai_router/session_state.py::_build_sessions_array, via
progress.heal_title) and the extension (utils/progress.ts::healTitle,
used by utils/sessionState.ts's synthesis and by the read-time heal in
normalizeToV4Shape). They disagreed in exactly the way this corpus now
forbids: the TypeScript side hardcoded `Session ${n}` while already
holding the spec's real titles, and because title resolution puts the
stored ledger FIRST, whichever writer got there first made its answer
permanent.
TWO suites assert against this file, and neither one owns it:
ai_router/tests/test_session_title_parity.py
drives progress.heal_title / heal_generic_titles directly, and
drives the real writer (_build_sessions_array) over an on-disk
spec.md for the end-to-end cases.
tools/dabbler-ai-orchestration/src/test/suite/sessionTitleParity.test.ts
drives utils/progress.ts's healTitle / healGenericTitles and the
extension's own synthesis over the same inputs.
So: change Python alone and the Python test fails. Change TypeScript
alone and the TypeScript test fails. Change this file alone and BOTH
fail. There is no edit that silently diverges the two.
THE RULE, in one line: a spec heading beats a generic-shaped stored
title (exactly `Session <that entry's own number>`, or empty); a
genuinely operator-authored title is never overwritten.
Field guide for `cases`:
name        — what the case pins, for the failure message.
storedTitle — the title already in sessions[] (null = no entry yet).
number      — the session number the entry carries.
specTitles  — {number: title} extracted from spec.md ({} = none).
expected    — the resolved title, or null when the rule resolves to
nothing and the caller's own `Session N` fallback wins.
isGeneric   — what the generic-shape predicate must say about
(storedTitle, number).
